original_question: For semidirect products G = C_p semidirect C_m with m prime to p, when does every G-crossed product over F descend to a crossed product for a smaller or more abelian group G'? In particular, is every division algebra of prime degree p that is split by C_p semidirect C_m necessarily cyclic, and are all quasi-symbols cyclic?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 2.6(1)–(2) in "Other problems regarding crossed products."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s descent problem for semidirect splitting groups of the form C_p ⋊ C_m with m prime to p, the associated cyclicity question for prime-degree algebras split by such a group, and the special quasi-symbol case.
missing_details: The paper’s official target in the special case is not an unspecified "smaller or more abelian" group G'; it is specifically the abelian group C_p × C_m.
One must specify that A is an F-division algebra of prime degree p and that K/F is a Galois splitting field for A with Gal(K/F) ≅ C_p ⋊ C_m.
The semidirect-product hypothesis includes that C_p is normal in C_p ⋊ C_m.
The paper introduces the notation G ⇒_F G' to mean that every G-crossed product whose center contains F is necessarily a G'-crossed product; your draft does not state this operator or its scope.
The quantifier over fields is part of the official problem: one is asked to determine the conditions on F under which the descent statement holds.
For the quasi-symbol clause, one must define quasi-symbol precisely: K^{C_p} = F(ζ_p) for a primitive p-th root of unity ζ_p; in particular char(F) ≠ p.
The nearby context explicitly states the equivalent reformulation of Problem 2.6(1): C_p ⋊ C_m ⇒_F C_p × C_m if and only if all F-algebras of prime degree p split by C_p ⋊ C_m are cyclic.

The broader quasi-symbol framework discussed nearby also introduces hypothesis (2.7) for degree p^r quasi-symbols; if one wants that stronger setting, it must be stated explicitly rather than left implicit.
refined_question: Let F be a field, and write G ⇒_F G' to mean that every G-crossed product whose center contains F is also a G'-crossed product. For a prime p and an integer m prime to p, with C_p normal in the semidirect product C_p ⋊ C_m, determine whether C_p ⋊ C_m ⇒_F C_p × C_m. In the particularly interesting case of a quasi-symbol—namely, an F-division algebra A of degree p split by a Galois extension K/F with Gal(K/F) ≅ C_p ⋊ C_m and K^{C_p} = F(ζ_p) for a primitive p-th root of unity ζ_p (so char(F) ≠ p)—must A be cyclic?
equivalent_formulation: For Problem 2.6(1), the paper states that C_p ⋊ C_m ⇒_F C_p × C_m if and only if every F-algebra of prime degree p that is split by C_p ⋊ C_m is cyclic.
justification: This draft is aiming at the "Descending from prime-to-p extensions" discussion in §2, not at Problem 1.1. The paper first sets up the prime-degree descent problem for algebras split by a Galois extension with group C_p ⋊ C_m, defines the special case of quasi-symbols by the condition K^{C_p} = F(ζ_p), and then states Problem 2.6 with exactly the two subquestions your draft is trying to capture: whether C_p ⋊ C_m ⇒_F C_p × C_m for m prime to p, and whether all quasi-symbols are cyclic. The immediately following context gives the explicit equivalence between 2.6(1) and the cyclicity of prime-degree F-algebras split by C_p ⋊ C_m, so your draft is substantially correct but needs the paper’s precise group target, operator meaning, field hypotheses, and quasi-symbol definition.
